lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.45 - A Listen and number

details: Listen and number checks students' recall of the target vocabulary from Units 3 and 4 (fruit and vegetables and animals), and gives them the opportunity to practise listening for detail.
Look for careful listening, accurate identification of the target vocabulary and correct numbering of the boxes.
“Let’s go to the zoo today. We can see the animals and find out what food they like.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.45 - B. Listen and choose

details: Listen and choose reviews the target language and key structures from Units 3 and 4 (fruit and vegetables, animals, Is it a…?, Do you like…?)) and offers a further opportunity to practise listening for detail.
Look for careful listening, accurate identification of the pictures based on the descriptions and correct circling of the letters.
“I love looking around the zoo. But I’ve forgotten the names of some of the animals and I don’t know what food they like. Can you help me listen and choose the correct answers?”

Heads Up:

Heads Down:

Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.97 - A Look and match

details: Look and match checks students' understanding of the key language at a sentence level and strengthens recognition of target words with word-picture matching reinforcing whole-word memory.
Look for students correctly identifying the images and  drawing lines to the correct sentences.
“Great work, but I forgot who likes which animals and what foods they eat. Can you help me match the pictures to the sentences?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.97 - B Look and write

details: Look and write strengthens recognition of target language and key structures and gives students an opportunity to practise spelling them. Writing the words in the appropriate spaces reinforces language chunk recall.
Look for correct word choice and spelling, consistent letter formation, neat handwriting within the lines and finger spacing between the words.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:
Show the Leaderboard and congratulate / encourage daily app practise.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.46 - C. Listen and read

details: Listen and read allows students to review the usage of ‘Do you like..?’, ‘I like…’ and short form answers, and the target language from Units 3 and 4, while practising their literacy skills.

Look for careful listening, students following the text (with their eyes, or a finger) while they listen, and clear pronunciation, steady pacing and correct identification of each word while they read.
“Look, Kate's class are going to the zoo today, too. Let’s listen and read and find out what animals they see and what they like to eat.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.

Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.46 - D. Choose the correct answers 10m]

details: Choose the correct answers checks students’ understanding of the text and gives them an opportunity to practise reading for understanding.
Look for correct circling/writing of the answers and the ability to identify where in the text they found the answers.
“I want to find out more about the elephants. Which one of Kate’s friends should I talk to?”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Chant): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video Chant): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4R

Diary:
